trial_title: Cefepime/AAI101 Phase 2 Study in Hospitalized Adults With cUTI
brief_summary:
Phase 2, randomised, double-blind, 2-cohort study in hospitalised adults with complicated urinary tract infection (cUTI), including acute pyelonephritis. All study cohorts were randomised in a 2:1 ratio. Treatment duration for each cohort was 7 to 10 days. Patients were not permitted to switch to oral therapy.

Cohort 1: 15 patients treated with cefepime 1 g/AAI101 500 mg intravenous (i.v.) infusion over 2 hours once every 8 hours (q8h), and 7 patients treated with cefepime 1 g i.v. infusion ove

eligibility_table.criterion: Male or female patients with clinical signs and/or symptoms of cUTI or acute pyelonephritis that were expected to require hospitalization and initial treatment with at least 7 days of i.v. antibiotics.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has complicated UTIs, but there is no indication that hospitalization and initial treatment with at least 7 days of i.v. antibiotics is expected.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patients with concurrent infection that would interfere with evaluation of response to the study antibiotics;
eligibility_table.justification: There is no concurrent infection reported that would interfere with the evaluation of response to study antibiotics.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patients needing concomitant systemic antimicrobial agents in addition to those designated in the various study treatment groups;
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is not reported to need any concomitant systemic antimicrobial agents.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patients receiving effective antibacterial drug therapy for any indication for a continuous duration of >24 hours during the previous 72 hours before the study-qualifying baseline urine was obtained or receiving any amount of potentially therapeutic antibacterial therapy after collection of the pre-treatment baseline urine culture and before administration of the first dose of study drug;
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a history of complicated UTIs and may have received antibacterial therapy recently, which could exceed the 24-hour limit.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patients likely to require the use of an antibiotic for cUTI or acute pyelonephritis prophylaxis during participation in the study;
eligibility_table.justification: Given the patient's history of complicated UTIs, there is a likelihood that she may require antibiotic prophylaxis during the study.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patients with confirmed fungal urinary tract infection at the screening visit (with ≥103 fungal colony forming units [CFU]/mL);
eligibility_table.justification: No lab values in patient profile
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a confirmed fungal urinary tract infection with ≥103 fungal colony forming units (CFU)/mL at the screening visit?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patients with intractable urinary infection at baseline that the Investigator anticipated would require >10 days of study drug therapy were excluded from participation
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's intractable urinary infection status is unclear, making it difficult to determine if >10 days of study drug therapy would be required.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the investigator's anticipated duration of study drug therapy for this patient expected to be >10 days?
